newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end mixed, losses pared.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end mixed, losses pared.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures continued to recover from early lows on local short covering and ended mixed with pared losses, traders said.

Liquidation in the December hog contract ahead of Friday's expiration provided the bulk of pressure in pork complex futures. Forecasts for warmer weather and expected larger hog marketings soon also weighed on futures.

However, early pressure, including fund selling, lacked follow through near 59.000 cents per lb in December and under 75.000 cents in February, traders said. Futures were starting to look oversold in light of estimates for next week's Hogs and Pigs report, they said.
The report is expected to show tight market numbers in the first quarter and then rising hog numbers through next year as producers have held back hogs for breeding, sources forecast.

Early estimates on the report pointed to all hogs on farms at 95 to 101 percent of a year ago with numbers kept for breeding estimated at 99.9 to 103 percent and hogs kept for marketing at 94 to 99 percent of last year.
